items.title: codebase-map
items.text: Multi-language systematic codebase mapping analysis (Python, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, SQL, PL/SQL, Rust, Go, CSS/SCSS/LESS) - analyzes architecture, traces data flows, detects anti-patterns, and generates structured documentation for onboarding, architecture review, or code documentation. Root of the review and documentation dependency graph: it also owns the semantic interconnect mapper (contracts / invariants / domain rules / assumptions) that team-review and project-knowledge both consume. Concurrent-safe: every analysis is an isolated run under .codebase-map/runs/ published to a stable root mirror. The Next Steps menu wires the output into downstream documentation generators (CLAUDE.md, codebase map, interface docs) as a technical-reference backbone. Renamed from deep-dive-analysis in 2.0.0. Runs are incremental: each records a structural snapshot of the tree it analyzed, and a later run diffs it against the worktree, carries unaffected claims forward and re-derives only what changed.

items.title: repo-hygiene
items.text: Workspace tidying decided by the filesystem and git alone, with no source comprehension anywhere in it: filesystem garbage and shell-redirection artifacts, generated artifacts tracked in git (checked against publication conventions before anything is proposed for untracking), .gitignore completeness per ecosystem and archaeology over stale and overly-broad rules with git check-ignore provenance, scratch and pipeline-output directories, orphan doc-assets widened past literal Markdown links to configs, stylesheets and templates, and git auxiliary state. One check catalog with a full and a lite profile, so the diff-scoped pass inside a code review and the whole-tree pass share definitions and cannot drift. Its tidy method, run by /daodan:tidy-repo, previews first and applies only with an authorization asked after the preview, with or without commits; untracked removals are quarantined rather than deleted, git rm --cached is confirmed per item, and the git-state dimension is permanently detection-only because a dropped stash or a removed worktree leaves no diff for a per-phase commit to revert.

items.title: graphify 0.9.97
items.text:
0.9.97 (2026-10-27)

Security: rationale redaction credential redaction for rationale labels moves to a single pre-cache choke point (_redact_rationale_labels inside _safe_extract), so no extractor can skip it, and it now covers more leak shapes: URL userinfo with an empty user or with //@ in the password, PEM private-key bodies, tokens glued to surrounding text by _ (for example ghp_...), Slack xoxe- refresh tokens, short JWTs, and Common Lisp docstrings that previously built labels without redacting. Benign strings (hashes, sk- prose, URLs without userinfo) are left alone (#4647, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).

Security: deps anyio is floored to >=4.14.2 in the mcp extra, above CVE-2026-63374 (an IDNA 2003 vs 2008 hostname-validation bypass that let a MITM on a non-ASCII domain present a cert for a different ASCII host, CVSS 9.3). anyio is only a transitive dependency and the lockfile already resolves 4.15.1, so this is a floor to stop a future re-resolution from regressing.

Fix: markdown ATX headings parse per CommonMark: a trailing run of # is not part of the heading text (## Setup ## is "Setup"), up to three spaces of indent are allowed (four is an indented code block), and a hash-only line like ## ## mints no node (#4790, #4791, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: markdown fenced code blocks are tracked by CommonMark rules (backtick and tilde fences, info strings, matching close length), so a line that looks like a heading inside a fence no longer leaks as structure, and a heading after a ~~~ block that contains a ``` line is no longer lost (#4787, #4788, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: yaml structural extraction reads the composed node tree, so keys carry their written spelling and their own source line instead of all landing on line 1, and YAML 1.1 bare keys like on/off/yes/no are no longer folded to booleans (a workflow on: block is extracted, not turned into a True node) (#4784, #4785, thanks @jaimemartinez).

Fix: razor a component's @implements interfaces are extracted as implements edges instead of being silently dropped (#4820, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: terraform an aliased provider block gets its own alias-qualified node (so two provider "aws" blocks no longer collapse into one and lose attributes), and a provider = aws.west reference resolves to it instead of dangling; a local literally named provider is no longer misread (#4819, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: cobol paragraphs that follow a nested END PROGRAM reattach to the enclosing program instead of sticking to the nested one, via a program stack (#4824, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: blade a wire:click directive binds the bare method name: dotted modifiers (wire:click.prevent="submit") are matched, call arguments are trimmed from the name (deleteItem(5) binds deleteItem), and a $-prefixed magic action mints no fabricated edge (#4823, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: pascal a record is recognised as a type with its own methods in the regex fallback (the default path without the optional pascal extra), matching the tree-sitter path; operator members are extracted too (#4825, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: vbnet an Operator declaration is extracted as an operator-kind member of its class and its body is walked for calls, so a helper call inside an operator no longer vanishes (#4821, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: fortran a call resolves to the subroutine it actually names instead of a target salted with the calling file's name (which never resolved), using the extractor's own cross-file stub idiom (#4795, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: cli graphify query --help/-h (and now graphify explain --help/-h) with nothing else prints usage instead of running a literal query for the text "--help"; a longer question that merely contains "--help" as a substring still runs as a query (#4830, thanks @curl-man).

Fix: js a nested (inner) function no longer leaks into the file-wide name map, so a call elsewhere in the file binds to the top-level function of that name rather than an inner one it cannot see; recursion, shadowing and sibling scopes resolve correctly (ports the Python scope scheme to JS/TS) (#4767, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: ocaml every binding in an and-chained module ... and ... or class ... and ... is extracted, not just the first, so later bindings are no longer silently dropped; each carries its own source line (#4822, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: verilog a SystemVerilog class task method is modeled like a function one (its own node, method edge and parameter-type references), and a task-local variable no longer leaks as a false field reference on the class (#4774, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: build an edge with no relation is dropped instead of persisted, on both the build and the raw --no-cluster write paths, and alias folding (relationship to relation) runs before the check (#4810, thanks @legendteddy; reproducer also filed as #4826 by @sunhouy).

Fix: build the shrink guard counts a saved document-mention node that folds into its AST file twin on reload as present, not lost, so a cluster-only write is no longer refused when nothing was actually lost (#4778, #4779, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

Fix: detect a linked git worktree whose main checkout resolves inside the scan root is pruned, so a sibling worktree no longer gets indexed as a second full copy of the repo (#4683, #4833, thanks @barlowa124; duplicate work in #4685 by @AndresDiagoM).

Fix: resolution an inline comment in a pnpm-workspace glob is stripped per YAML rules, and a glob that Path.glob rejects (a ** component or an absolute pattern) is skipped with a warning instead of crashing the whole extract run (#4681, #4687, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: report a community hub [[wikilink]] is slugged through the same export._obsidian_safe_stem the export uses, so the link matches the file the export actually writes instead of dangling (#4696, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: wiki a community relabelled only by letter case keeps its article instead of having the sweep delete the file the run just wrote; on a case-sensitive filesystem the stale lower-case twin is unlinked rather than renamed over the fresh file (which would silently restore the old body) (#4508, #4798, thanks @dupeisen).

Fix: query filler verbs get/gets/got/getting are dropped from query terms (like the existing work/works), so a framework hub labelled "Get" is not pulled in as a BFS seed by an exact-match bonus; node lookups for a literal Get still resolve (#4686, thanks @AndresDiagoM).

items.title: graphify 0.9.96
items.text:
0.9.96 (2026-10-25)

Security: deps the Pillow floor is raised to >=13.0.0 on Python 3.11+ (staying at >=12.3.0 on 3.10, which Pillow 13 no longer supports) and pypdf to >=6.19.0, and the lockfile is refreshed to patched versions of transitive dependencies (pyjwt, cryptography, certifi, urllib3, anyio, fsspec, soupsieve, virtualenv). This clears the bulk of the open Dependabot advisories; the Pillow image-parsing CVEs are only patched upstream for Python 3.11+, so a 3.10 install keeps the newest 3.10-compatible Pillow.

Fix: llm a chunk that failed before returning a response no longer has its files reported as model omissions; the warning distinguishes a failed chunk from a genuine omission, and both are still re-dispatched (#3616, #4752, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @GREYGROUPJP).

Fix: watch a Markdown file that detect() classifies as a paper (arXiv markers, an Abstract) is included in the watch quick-scan rebuild instead of contributing zero nodes; a paper that already has a semantic layer is still excluded from the AST quick-scan (#4750, #4751, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @yeochul-jeon).

Fix: prs every unfinished CheckRun status (WAITING, REQUESTED, PENDING, ...) counts as pending CI, so a PR gated on a deployment-protection job is no longer read as ready (#4730, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: export an Obsidian note lists every parallel relation between two nodes (for example both imports and calls) instead of only the first edge (#4731, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: build a hyperedge whose members are given under the members/node_ids aliases has its numeric member ids coerced to strings like the canonical nodes list, so the hyperedge is no longer dropped (#4732, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: llm a code node whose confidence is written in a different case (extracted/Extracted) is still evidence-checked before it folds to the EXTRACTED enum, so an un-verified node is not presented as solid (#4733, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: python a member call binds to the method it actually spells rather than a case/underscore-folded twin (run() no longer resolves to _run()); a lone folded method still resolves, and a genuine collision fails closed (#4734, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: zig a call no longer crosses between a method and a same-named free function; a bare call binds the free function and a receiver call binds the method (#4755, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: dart an unnamed extension on T { } declaration is detected and extracted (the name is optional), so its members attach to the extended type (#4741, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: llm the DeepSeek backend sends its output cap as max_tokens (which DeepSeek honours) rather than max_completion_tokens (which it ignores), so responses are no longer silently uncapped (#4739, #4753, thanks @Ethereal49; reported by @snapp-kenya).

Fix: extract XAML codebehind (*.xaml to *.xaml.cs) resolves deterministically regardless of directory iteration order, so a graph built on a case-sensitive filesystem is stable (#4747, thanks @anishraja04).

Fix: extract the AST cache hit rate is reported over the file total, not the uncached set, so a warm run no longer prints a misleading "100% uncached" line (#4740, #4746, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @lavaxun).

Fix: dedup a node id legitimately shared by two files as a module/namespace no longer prints a spurious "minted by two different files" warning (#4756, thanks @idachev).

Fix: python the member-call resolver binds only Python callers to Python targets, so a same-named class in another language is no longer mis-bound as a call (#4757, thanks @idachev).

Fix: cli the PreToolUse hook reminders are worded as facts rather than imperatives, so the agent's tool-result stream no longer reads them as prompt injection and ignores them (#2202, #4764, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: llm the Ollama context window is sized from an estimate that counts non-Latin characters as whole tokens and from the real system-prompt length, so a non-English or long prompt is no longer silently truncated (#4414, #4761, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: cli graphify extract records each run's token usage to graphify-out/cost.json (the same ledger the skill writes), so a standalone extract refresh updates the cost history (#1769, #4765, thanks @smngvlkz).

Fix: ts chained TypeScript decorators (@(Link().toMany())) are recovered as a decorator reference, and a lossy-parse warning names the real error region (#4711, #4715, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: js a const X = require('pkg') binding for an external package keeps its node (with the package as source) so new X() still resolves, while a require of a corpus-local file still folds to the required module (#4688, #4702, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: detect generated MSBuild obj/ and bin/ output is pruned only when build evidence is present (restore/runtime markers nearby), so a C# project scanned after a build no longer ingests generated sources while a real src/bin stays (#4742, thanks @Great-Peace).

Fix: watch each watch rebuild is bounded by GRAPHIFY_REBUILD_TIMEOUT (default 600s, 0 disables), with a thread-Timer fallback where SIGALRM is unavailable or watch() runs off the main thread (a SIGALRM arm there raises ValueError and would tear the watcher down before the rebuild ran), so a hung rebuild no longer stalls the watcher (#2173, #4724, thanks @danieldutu).

Fix: robot each duplicate test-case name gets its own node (salted by line), so two tests with the same name are kept distinct (#4697, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: vbnet external namespaces and types emit a sourceless stub carrying an empty source_file sentinel like other languages, instead of a node that fails validation (#4725, #4728, thanks @madanlalit; reported by @alopezradicle).

Fix: rust a use is scoped to the crate it names, so use serde_json::Value no longer resolves to a same-named type in another crate; a named pub use re-export is followed and a manifest-less binding stays INFERRED (#4699, #4712, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: python a call through a field injected from a constructor parameter, or through a local typed by a method's return annotation, resolves to the target method (INFERRED); it requires a single unambiguous producer and class (#4726, thanks @keny11300).

Fix: dedup an LLM-marked cross-document reference stub that collides with its real definition is namespaced instead of silently dropped, so neither node is lost (#4738, #4743, thanks @SinghAman21; reported by @snapp-kenya).

items.title: Autopilot, dashboard inbox, editor agent skills, and more
items.text:
Autopilot

Autopilot (beta): Autopilot is a proactive agent that opens pull requests to keep your documentation up-to-date, and performs ongoing maintenance such as a daily quality check. Turn it on from the Autopilot page in your dashboard. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Review suggestions: Autopilot's pull requests appear under Suggestions, where you can preview, accept, close, or ask for changes in a chat. See Review suggestions.

Feature launches: For a large launch, Autopilot tracks the feature and keeps a draft pull request current until the code merges. See Feature launches.

Integration events: Ask Autopilot in a chat to run when an event happens in a connected shared integration, such as a new Linear issue. See Slack and other integrations.

Signed commits: GitHub signs Autopilot's commits and shows them as Verified, so they work with branch protection rules that require signed commits. See How Autopilot opens pull requests.

Editor and dashboard

Agent skills: Add reusable instructions that the agent loads when a request matches them. Create skills, upload SKILL.md files, .skill or .zip archives, or folders, or ask the agent to save a skill while you chat. Admins can move personal skills to your organization.

Inbox: The inbox collects replies, mentions in comments and page content, comments on pages you own, and shared private pages. Filter by section and date range, and mark everything as read at once.

Edits from comment threads: Ask @mintlify in a comment to change a page and the agent performs edits then updates the comment thread. See Ask the Mintlify agent.

Show all branches: Choose whether the branch menu lists every branch in your repository. See Show all branches.

Commit co-authors: Credit teammates as co-authors on editor commits. See Editor settings.

Delete agent chats: Delete chats from the agent's session history.

Source mode: Fold component blocks and code fences and keep your scroll position when you switch between visual and source mode. JSX attribute expressions highlight as JavaScript, and style objects autocomplete CSS properties and describe them on hover.

Mermaid diagrams: Visual mode hides Mermaid code by default and remembers whether you show it.

Inline SVG and custom pages: Visual mode draws inline <svg> blocks. On pages in custom or frame mode, components respond to clicks and you can select and copy text.

Page titles in URLs: Editor URLs and copied page links include the page title, such as /~/Getting-Started-<id>. Existing links still work.

Copy and move pages: The page menu's Copy to… and Move to… options are now Copy to a project and Move within project. After you copy a page to another project, the editor opens the copy. See Copy a page to another project.

Billing page: Set overages and spend limits for each project and compare plans on the redesigned Billing page. On Pro and Enterprise plans, reserve credits for a project. See Overages.

Automations in project settings: Automations moved to your project settings.

Desktop app

Copy tab links: Right-click a tab and select Copy Link to copy the link to its page.

What's new: See recent changes to the desktop app in its settings.

Published sites

Page styles: Add a <style> block to a page to style only that page's content. See Custom CSS.

Styling hooks: Style the search bar, search dialog, and theme layout with stable data-search-item and data-layout-item attributes. Log in and log out links in the sidebar have the login-link and logout-link classes, like the links in the navigation bar. See Class and element hooks.

JSON request bodies: Switch between Form and JSON to edit request bodies in the API playground. See Edit request bodies as JSON.

Optional API fields: Set api.optional to collapse, expand, or always show optional fields in the API playground. See API settings.

Markdown export: .md pages render components, Visibility content, and snippets as plain Markdown, and keep the text of components such as Frame, Tile, and Prompt. Links to pages in your navigation point to their .md versions, and on most sites internal links use your site's full URL. See Components and HTML.

Go SDK references: Generate SDK reference pages for Go packages with the go format and mintlify-go-extractor. See Go.

Javadoc navigation: SDK reference navigation for Javadoc artifacts groups symbols by kind within each package. See Generated pages.

Classic thumbnails: Generated OG images use the classic layout by default. Thumbnails with a custom background image and no preset keep their original layout. See thumbnails.

Google Fonts from your domain: On sites without authentication, Mintlify serves Google Fonts from your docs domain, so readers' browsers don't connect to Google.

Assistant widget text size: Set appearance.fontSize to a number from 12 to 20 to change the text size of the assistant widget in pixels.

Preview access through the API: Pass auth to the Trigger preview deployment endpoint to protect a preview with a password or dashboard login.

Old previews: If you change your repository, Mintlify deletes previews from the previous repository after seven days. See Preview lifetime.

CLI

Generate docs.json files: mint dev generates a docs.json file from your folder structure when your directory doesn't have one. See Local preview.

Preview on other devices: mint dev listens only on localhost. To open the preview on a phone or another computer, run mint dev --host. See Preview on other devices.

Breaking change

mint test removed: The CLI no longer includes the mint test command. Remove it from scripts and CI workflows that call it.

AI and MCP

Admin MCP editing: edit_page applies up to 100 replacements in one call, create_node writes into a page that already exists at the path, and write_page and edit_page report markup the editor drops. See Content.

Admin MCP navigation: list_nodes returns fewer fields for each node and leaves out uploaded files unless you filter for them. Update scripts that read other fields. list_deployments returns each project's projectType. See Navigation.

Admin MCP deploy status: deployment_status reports whether published changes are live, and suggest_edit accepts a comment that explains the change. See Branches and publishing.

Bring your own model: Starter questions and the commit messages and pull request details for editor publishes also run on your key. See Bring your own model. Available on Enterprise plans.

API request examples: When readers ask the assistant how to call an API, its answers include a minimal request example based on your docs.

Assistant API limits: The assistant API no longer has a per-IP daily request limit. See Create assistant message.

Conversation IDs: Assistant conversation exports include a conversationId that groups turns from the same conversation. See Assistant conversations.

Bug fixes

Editor: Imported .md files parse as Markdown, and Notion Markdown exports are cleaned up on import. HTML links to sections on the same page scroll in visual mode. Bold and italic formatting stays after you post a comment. New branches no longer reuse names of deleted branches. Interrupted agent responses reconnect. OpenAPI page descriptions render components. Typing --- in source mode starts frontmatter. Template literals inside HTML no longer gain indentation when you save, and inline HTML tables keep their layout when you click a cell.

Published sites: Switching versions keeps you on the same page when the other version files it elsewhere. Price-like dollar amounts render as text instead of math. Scrolling in Safari continues over horizontal scrollbars. MCP discovery documents use your custom domain. On sites with authentication, the contextual menu's MCP options point to the authenticated MCP server. RSS items keep their original dates. Tailwind classes passed through variables and expressions get their styles.

API playground: Request examples use server variable defaults when the playground is hidden. Requests without a body sent through the playground proxy no longer fail with 415 errors.

Previews: View Preview links open the preview's home page when the linked page isn't in the build. Leftover previews from a previous repository no longer block new previews.

Offline exports: API playground icons load from the export.

Desktop app: Switching organizations no longer reloads every tab. Tabs show the editor branch, and new tabs keep your theme.

Dashboard: Visit page stays disabled until your site's first build is live. Pending custom domains appear in your custom domain settings. Choosing no spend limit no longer turns off overages. Projects you delete leave the project list right away, and a new project that reuses a deleted project's subdomain starts with an empty editor.

Automations: Scheduled Update from code changes runs no longer skip commits that are pushed after their commit date.

items.title: graphify 0.9.95
items.text:
Twenty-one community pull requests. A security pass on install: the skill-install writes go through randomly-named temp files instead of predictable ones, so a pre-planted symlink can no longer redirect a write. Extraction: Python, Go, C++ and Rust explicit type aliases (and Rust union items) are extracted as type nodes so references resolve instead of minting sourceless stubs, each C# method overload gets its own node bound by argument count, and a package.json dependency's manifest entry links to the node that references it. Plus a one-root-per-repo tree on merged graphs, extended-length cache paths on Windows, and binary media no longer counted as text. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: security the skill install stages every write (version stamp, SKILL.md, references) through a randomly-named mkstemp/mkdtemp file created with O_EXCL and restrictive mode instead of a predictable *.tmp name, so a local attacker who pre-creates a symlink at that path can no longer redirect the write to clobber an arbitrary file; the final move stays atomic (#4513, thanks @Mahdifotohi).

Fix: python an explicit module-level type alias (X: TypeAlias = ..., type X = ..., NewType) is extracted as a type node, so a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless stub; an implicit assignment, a local alias, or a re-export is left alone (#4578, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: go a type A = B alias is extracted as a type node (tree-sitter parses it as a type_alias, not a type_spec), so references resolve to it; a re-export (type Field = pkg.Field) mints no node (#4579, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: cpp a namespace-scope using A = B; or typedef B A; alias is extracted as a type node so references resolve; a member alias inside a class and a same-name re-export are excluded (#4580, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: rust a type alias and a union item are extracted as type nodes (a union's fields reference their types like a struct), so references resolve instead of minting stubs; an impl-associated type is excluded (#4581, Refs #4285, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik; reported by @jonatasbcardio-boop).

Fix: csharp each method overload gets its own node and source location instead of collapsing to one, and a call binds to the overload matching its argument count, across in-file, receiver-typed, bare-name cross-file, partial-class, and interface-dispatch resolution; a non-overloaded method keeps its id (#4584, #4591, thanks @Mpasha17; reported by @TerraVenil).

Fix: tree graphify export tree on a merged multi-repo graph gives each repo its own root (keyed by the repo tag) instead of conflating same-path files from different repos; untagged nodes are not counted as a repo (#4524, #4525, thanks @AromalBiju1).

Fix: cache AST cache entries are read and written through Windows extended-length (\\?\) paths, so a deep cache path over the 260-character limit no longer fails extraction with a FileNotFoundError; a no-op off Windows (#4542, thanks @omsenjalia).

Fix: detect a binary media file (an image or audio/video) is no longer read and counted as text toward the corpus word total; an SVG stays counted as the XML text it is (#4548, thanks @kalkaran).

Fix: json_config a package.json dependency's manifest entry links (declares) to the ref node that importing code resolves to, so the manifest entry and its importers share one node instead of being orphaned; the entry is relabelled name@range (#4569, #4572, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @BiSide).

Feature: yaml .yaml/.yml files are now extracted structurally (a file node plus contains edges to keys) and classified as code rather than documents, so Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, and CI pipelines contribute nodes to a code-only or --update run instead of nothing, matching how .json is handled. Multi-document streams (--- separators) are walked per document; a data array, an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, a JSON-schema-in-YAML, and a flat data bundle are skipped so data-heavy YAML does not mint orphan nodes; parsing uses safe_load so a !!python/... tag never executes; output is bounded (1 MiB, 500 pairs, depth 6). The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#2214, #4706, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @dchavezf).

Fix: extract a bare call that resolves to a same-named symbol only because the caller imported that symbol's module (from b import other, then a call to a _make_id defined in both a.py and b.py) is no longer promoted to EXTRACTED; the edge is still emitted for connectivity but stays INFERRED, so a symbol that was never imported is not falsely certified. A real symbol import (from a import _make_id) still resolves EXTRACTED (#2945, #4707, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @TotalUnitManagement).

Fix: security the SSRF guard blocks a host that resolves to a multicast address (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8), closing a gap alongside the existing private/reserved/loopback/link-local checks (#4708, thanks @Dextheking1).

Fix: security the Obsidian export sanitizes a node's file-type and confidence before emitting them as frontmatter tags, so a crafted value cannot break out of the YAML list into a sibling key, matching how community tags are already sanitized (#4709, thanks @Dextheking1).

Fix: security the Google Workspace shortcut sidecar escapes a file id or url through full YAML double-quoted-scalar escaping (tab, C0/DEL controls, and the Unicode line breaks U+2028/U+2029/U+0085), so a hostile shortcut file cannot inject frontmatter keys (#4710, thanks @Dextheking1).

Fix: affected graphify affected <path> resolves a path whose file-node label was disambiguated by the shared-basename suffix pass (for example two hooks.py from different directories), reusing the canonical file-label predicate instead of a bare basename match (#4698, #4713, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @karsan8119).

Fix: build a raw (--no-cluster) build resolves an import endpoint through the same old-stem alias index the clustered build uses, and mints an external stub only after resolution, so the raw graph no longer freezes an import onto a stub when the clustered graph resolves it (#4670, #4676, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @xiongjianxu).

Fix: cross-repo an Objective-C class declared in one repo's header and implemented in another repo's .m binds a member call to the implementation, the cross-repo analog of the same-repo split-dir fix; two same-named classes that both define the selector stay ambiguous (#4690, #4691, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: hooks the rebuild hook runs from the checkout's top level (derived from the git common dir, falling back to --show-toplevel), so a stray graphify-out/ in a subdirectory can no longer root the rebuild at the wrong place and walk an enormous tree (#3258, #4689, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @dsfaccini).

Fix: objc NS_CLOSED_ENUM declarations are extracted as enums with their cases, the same as NS_ENUM/NS_OPTIONS; the AST cache schema is bumped so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#4705, thanks @Jvxoq).

Fix: sql a CREATE TABLE whose column default the SQL grammar cannot parse (for example MySQL/MariaDB DEFAULT current_timestamp()) is recovered from the ERROR node instead of being dropped, so the table and its foreign-key references still resolve; the AST cache schema is bumped (#4613, #4677, thanks @08raviyadav; reported by @AirRunner).

items.title: graphify 0.9.94
items.text:
Nineteen community pull requests. A security pass on ingestion: a fetched URL with no hostname, with a malformed or zero port, or with embedded user:pass@ credentials is now rejected before the request leaves, on the first fetch and on every redirect, and a text capture no longer follows a dangling symlink out of the corpus. Extraction and resolution: a Maven POM contributes only its own dependencies, a JS/TS member call on an untyped receiver stops guessing a same-named method in the same file, a CommonJS require binding no longer shadows the class the required file exports, and Objective-C category node ids stay repo-relative instead of embedding the absolute checkout path. SQL gets its own pass: T-SQL bracketed names are unbracketed, a GO batch separator ends the statement, cross-file table stubs fold onto their real definition, and a procedure emits reads_from/writes_to edges. Plus a markdown bare method only links when its class is cited, the MCP node lookup refuses a substring near-miss instead of answering with an unrelated node, a cross-repo edge points at the call site, Objective-C calls resolve across a split header/impl, an incremental build stops re-queuing files an extractor declined by design, a quoted Codex hook command for install paths with spaces, an IPv6 bracketed-Host serve fix, and a complete, drift-guarded --platform list in --help. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: security validate_url rejects a fetched URL that has no hostname (http:///path), a non-numeric, out-of-range, or zero port, or embedded user:pass@ credentials, before the request is made and again on every redirect, so a malformed or credential-bearing URL is no longer fetched or persisted into the graph; a normal @ in a path or query and a valid high port still pass (#4643, #4644, #4645, thanks @cellrishi-code).

Fix: manifest a Maven pom.xml contributes only its own <dependencies> (including those under <profiles>), not the version pins under <dependencyManagement> or a build plugin's own <dependencies>, so a parent or BOM POM no longer emits dependency edges it only manages (#4596, thanks @jayhemnani9910).

Fix: js a member call on an untyped receiver (x.foo() where x has no known type) is deferred to receiver-typed resolution instead of binding to a same-named method elsewhere in the file, so a spurious self-loop or cross-call edge is no longer emitted; this.foo(), a typed receiver, and a locally instantiated receiver still resolve (#4598, #4605, thanks @ayushcodes10; reported by @SaschaAndresGrimm).

Fix: js a CommonJS const X = require('./m') binding no longer mints a module-scope node that shadows the class the required file exports, so new X() resolves to the required declaration; a real const x = factory() binding still keeps its node (#4621, #4634, thanks @lab1207; reported by @sub4biz).

Fix: extract an Objective-C category's class and method node ids stay repo-relative instead of embedding the absolute checkout path, so a category file like Foo+Cat.h yields portable ids that match across machines and merge cleanly; two same-named categories in different directories stay distinct (#4666, #4642, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik; reported by @xiongjianxu).

Fix: codex the generated Codex PreToolUse hook command quotes the graphify executable path, so an install under a path containing a space no longer builds a broken hook command, matching the existing Claude and Gemini hooks (#4662, thanks @supercell02).

Fix: serve an IPv6 HTTP bind accepts its own bracketed Host header ([::1]:port), so a server bound to an IPv6 loopback no longer refuses every request with a 421 (#4656, thanks @zydo).

Fix: ingest a text capture never writes through an existing entry: the free-path search uses lstat, so a name that is a dangling symlink is treated as occupied and the capture is diverted instead of following the link and writing outside the corpus (#4657, thanks @zydo).

Fix: cli graphify --help lists every accepted --platform value (it had omitted amp, copilot, kilo, kimi, and antigravity-windows); the list is derived from the same source as the install usage so the two cannot drift, with a guard test (#4655, thanks @zydo).

Fix: sql T-SQL bracketed identifiers ([dbo].[Orders]) are unbracketed so a name matches across styles, and a stored procedure's body emits reads_from/writes_to edges for the tables it reads and writes; aliases, variables, temp tables, strings, and comments never become targets (#4635, #4649, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @RuVl).

Fix: sql a GO batch separator (a client command, not a terminator) ends the statement, so a statement after a GO with no trailing ; parses on its own instead of merging into one malformed node; a GO inside a string, comment, or column name is left alone (#4651, #4652, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: sql a table referenced before its CREATE TABLE is seen folds onto the real definition instead of staying a separate stub, and a schema-qualified name binds correctly, while two genuinely different tables in different schemas (dbo.Orders vs sales.Orders) stay distinct and a SQL stub no longer binds to a same-named class in another language (#4653, #4654, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: markdown a bare method name in prose (for example redis where only Cache.redis exists) only links to the method when the owning class is cited in the same document, so a plain word is no longer turned into a false references edge; a qualified Class.method or Class::method mention still resolves (#4609, #4617, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @saad-siddique).

Fix: mcp the get_node and get_neighbors tools, and the explain command, refuse a substring-only near-miss with candidate suggestions instead of returning an unrelated node as the answer; an exact or prefix match still resolves (#3917, #4618, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @Alexandre-Aktisea).

Fix: cross-repo a cross-repo call edge points at the real call site rather than the caller's header declaration, so the edge's source_file and source_location name the line that makes the call (#4668, #4669, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: extract an incremental build no longer re-queues, on every run, a code file an extractor declined by design (for example a virtual-workspace manifest); the file is marked ast_empty and left alone, while a genuinely failed or transiently empty extraction is still retried (#2543, #4672, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: objc a member call resolves when a class is split across a header and an implementation in different directories, binding the selector to its single definition; two unrelated same-named classes that both define the selector stay ambiguous and get no edge (#4673, #4674, thanks @xiongjianxu).

items.title: graphify 0.9.93
items.text:
Twenty-two community pull requests. Extraction: a reference to a Kotlin type alias, C# delegate, Swift macro, Dart typedef, Python module function or Rust sibling-module use now resolves to its real declaration instead of minting a sourceless stub; Metal/CUDA GPU qualifiers no longer mint god nodes; extern "C" headers route to the C++ extractor; an extensionless script with a versioned-interpreter shebang is classified; and Obsidian vault-relative wikilinks resolve. Plus a credential-redaction pass on rationale labels, a node-confidence fold, a truncated-reply label decode, a .graphifyrc BOM fix, a GraphML multigraph export fix, two-repo file disambiguation in explain and path, a PDF-read warning, no skill writes on --version/--help, two PR-tooling fixes (slashed default branch, legacy CI statuses), and a skill partly-read-file recovery so a long file a subagent only skimmed is retried on the next --update instead of silently kept half-read. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: Kotlin a typealias declaration is extracted, so a field or parameter typed as the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless cross-file stub (#4553, #4557, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: C# a delegate declaration is extracted, so references resolve to it instead of a sourceless stub; built-in Func<>/Action<> stay external (#4552, #4556, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Swift macro declarations are extracted and a freestanding #macro(...) call resolves to the declaration; an unknown or standard-library macro stays unresolved rather than minting a stub (#4551, #4555, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: Rust a use rooted at a sibling mod (for example use item::Thing;) now reaches its declaration, while an external use serde::... still does not hijack a same-named local type (#4564, #4567, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @almothafar-maf).

Fix: build a node's drifted or legacy confidence is folded onto the enum the same way edges and hyperedges already are, so a node no longer reaches graph.json with an unnormalized confidence (#4529, #4531, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).

Fix: llm community labels salvaged from a truncated reply are JSON-decoded, so an escaped label (\", \n, \uXXXX, surrogate pairs) is no longer kept with literal backslash escapes (#4537, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: rcfile .graphifyrc is read as utf-8-sig, so a file saved with a UTF-8 BOM no longer drops its first key (#4538, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: Dart a typedef is extracted as a type alias on its own line, including the legacy typedef R name(args) form, instead of a bogus variable of type typedef; a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it rather than minting a sourceless typedef stub (#4582, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: Python a module.func() call resolves to the module child named exactly func, even when a same-key sibling (for example a FuncSchema class beside a func_schema function) previously made the lookup ambiguous and dropped the edge; it never binds to a same-named child of an unrelated module (#4577, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).

Fix: C++ Metal and CUDA GPU address/execution-space qualifiers (kernel, device, constant, __global__, __device__, ...) in a .metal/.cu file no longer mint sourceless god nodes; the kernel function still extracts and a <<<...>>> launch still resolves (#4550, #4554, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Fix: extract a .h header containing extern "C" is routed to the C++ extractor, so a C-API header the C grammar rejects extracts its symbols instead of nothing (#4526, thanks @bekzodibragimov2004-design).

Fix: extract credential-shaped text (API keys, tokens, Bearer tokens, private-key headers, user:pass@ URLs) in a comment or docstring that becomes a rationale label is redacted before it reaches graph.json, the viz or exports; ordinary identifiers such as git SHAs and UUIDs are left intact (#4566, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).

Fix: export GraphML export of a graph loaded as a MultiGraph (a graph with parallel edges, after #4500) no longer crashes with an empty output; parallel edges are written with distinct keys and round-trip through read_graphml (#4536, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: prs the default branch is derived by stripping only the refs/remotes/origin/ prefix, so a branch name that contains a slash (for example release/2.x) is kept whole and PRs against it are no longer all dropped as wrong-base (#4534, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: prs CI classification now reads legacy commit-status StatusContext state in addition to check-run conclusions, so a PR whose only signal is an external status (Jenkins, CircleCI) is classified correctly, with a failing status taking precedence (#4533, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: detect an extensionless script whose shebang names a versioned interpreter (#!/usr/bin/env python3.11, #!/bin/bash5, ruby3.2, ...) is now classified to its language instead of being skipped (#4535, thanks @rudycelekli).

Fix: detect when a PDF cannot be read (corrupt, encrypted, or a missing optional dependency) graphify prints a one-time warning naming the file instead of silently returning empty text, so a failed read is distinguishable from a text-less PDF (#4527, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).

Fix: markdown an Obsidian [[wikilink]] whose target begins with one of the scan root's own folder names (a vault-relative path) now resolves to the real page instead of a ghost node, restoring intra-vault connectivity (#4559, thanks @bercedev; reported by @CryptoRMac4).

Fix: explain / path two same-path files from different repos in a merged graph are kept distinct: an ambiguous name names each repo and the retry hint points at the full node id, instead of conflating them as one file (#4512, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @kaka-in-home).

Fix: cli graphify --version and --help no longer rewrite or back up an installed skill file; only a real command refreshes skills (the staleness warning still prints) (#4545, thanks @bercedev; reported by @EmanuelFaria).

Fix: query a bare name that is the exact name of several nodes (for example a .nonce() method in two files) is refused with the candidates listed and the ambiguous exit code, matching explain and path; a keyword that only prefix- or substring-matches labels still runs a normal search (#4511, #4517, thanks @shivampal46011; reported by @kaka-in-home).

Fix: skill a long file a subagent only partly read is no longer a silent, permanent loss. On the skill extraction path each chunk now self-reports the lines it covered; a file whose reported coverage falls short of its real length is written to .graphify_partial.txt, cached as partial (which the loader treats as a miss) and left unstamped in the manifest, so the next --update re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the half-read node set for a complete one. This mirrors the library path's truncated-reply recovery (#933, #1950); the already-extracted nodes are kept, and a file no subagent reported is not falsely flagged (#3987, #2225, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @Ryanm218).

Custom landing pages

Minor release adding a customizable page at the MCP URL with landing.tsx, plus agent streaming, OAuth client, and CLI fixes.

New (server, @mcp-use/cli): a landing.tsx in the MCP root replaces the page a browser sees at the MCP URL. mcp-use dev and mcp-use build find it (also under --mcp-dir) and mcp-use start serves the built page. It renders on the server and hydrates in the browser; without it, the built-in page is served as before (#2648)

New (server): mcp-use/landing exports React-free hooks for the page: useServerInfo(), useToolList(), usePromptList(), useResourceList() and useInstallTargets(). Server info always ships to the page; each list ships only when the page's import graph uses its hook (#2648)

New (server): getInstallTargets({ url, name }) returns install links and commands for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, VS Code Insiders, ChatGPT and the Manufact Inspector, for use outside the server such as on a docs site (#2648)

New (server): landing.tsx can export const metadata (title, description, icon, image) to set the page title, meta description, and Open Graph and Twitter tags (#2648)

New (@mcp-use/cli): Tailwind classes work in landing.tsx without a CSS file and CSS imports are bundled. In dev, edits use Fast Refresh, adding or deleting landing.tsx switches pages live, and a broken edit keeps serving the last working page. Builds honor MCP_ASSETS_URL (#2648)

New (create-mcp-use-app): every template includes a Tailwind-styled landing.tsx; blank and mcp-server add React and its types, and every template's tsconfig.json typechecks landing.tsx (#2648)

Fix (server, @mcp-use/cli): landing pages set data-theme from the OS color scheme before first paint so dark: classes work; a page whose CSS imports Tailwind itself owns Tailwind; and in mcp-use dev the page's stylesheets load before hydration (#2880)

Update (server): ChatGPT install steps follow the Plugins flow (Plugins → Add → Add Custom MCP Server) instead of developer mode and the Connectors tab (#2648)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use start --with-inspector serves the Inspector at /inspector when basePath is "/", and mcp-use dev prints /inspector instead of //inspector (#2555)

Fix (@mcp-use/cli): mcp-use client and mcp-use screenshot install a matching @mcp-use/client when they auto-install it, including on Windows where the install always failed (#2853)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): the OpenAI Responses provider emits tool-call argument events, so MCPAgent.stream() and streamEvents() report steps for tool calls on OpenAI models (#2551)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): MCPAgent.stream() returns and saves to memory only the final turn's text, the same as run(), instead of gluing on text written before tool calls (#2723)

Fix (@mcp-use/agent): RemoteAgent.run no longer rejects successful responses whose body has no error field, and error messages show the error instead of [object Object] (#2651)

Fix (@mcp-use/client): useMcp().authTokens.expires_at no longer moves later on every reconnect for opaque (non-JWT) tokens; the expiry is saved when tokens are received (#2879)

Fix (@mcp-use/client): Node OAuth loopback connections close after the callback, cancellation, or timeout, so the process can exit (#2766)

Update: Updated @mcp-use/cli to v4.5.0, create-mcp-use-app to v2.1.0, @mcp-use/client to v2.4.5, and @mcp-use/agent to v2.0.25

items.title: API reference pages in the editor, Admin MCP improvements, and more
items.text:
Breaking changes

Mintlify Index discontinued: The Index API returns 410 Gone and the Index MCP server tells connected agents to remove it. The dashboard no longer shows Index API keys, and the CLI no longer includes the mint index command.

Admin MCP tool changes: The admin MCP renames save to publish. Tools that edit content require a branch argument, and create_branch, discard, and status replace checkout, discard_session, and get_session_state. Dedicated project management tools replace the search_code_operations and execute_code code mode tools. Update prompts or scripts that call the old tools.

OpenAPI and API playground

OpenAPI 3.2: Mintlify accepts OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Tag hierarchies become nested navigation groups, and the API playground supports 3.2 additions such as the QUERY method and whole query string parameters. To upgrade a 3.1 document, change its openapi version.

Streaming responses: The API playground shows streaming responses as they arrive. Click Stop to end the request.

Editor and dashboard

API reference pages in the editor: Pages with openapi or api frontmatter show their endpoint and generated fields in the editor, so you can edit the content around them. See Pages.

Section links: Links to /page#heading open the page at that heading. Copy link to section in the block actions menu copies a dashboard link to the heading, and pasted section links show the section name.

Thumbnail settings: Set thumbnail overrides in page settings and in the settings for groups, tabs, and other navigation sections. See Edit page settings.

Unpublished site configuration: The site configuration view lists the sections with unpublished changes in a banner and marks them in the sidebar.

Print a page: Press Cmd + P to print the page content without the editor interface. See Keyboard shortcuts.

Agent mentions: Ask the agent to add teammate and page mentions to your content.

Haiku 5.5: Choose Haiku 5.5 in the agent's model picker.

Publishes: The Activity section of the dashboard is now Publishes, with Overview and Previews pages. See Deployments.

Admin MCP in the sidebar: Admin MCP settings and credentials have their own MCP item in the dashboard sidebar. Search MCP client credentials moved to the Docs MCP section of your project settings.

Regional translation targets: The Translate content automation can translate into British, Australian, and Canadian English and into Mexican and Latin American Spanish. See Manage automations.

Published sites

OG image presets: Choose a classic, headline, or minimal layout for generated OG images, with custom fonts, a brand or neutral background, and an eyebrow label above the title. Override the settings for individual pages and sections. See thumbnails.

Preview OG images: Run mint og to render a page's OG image to a PNG file.

Visibility by sign-in state and group: Show content only to signed-in readers, signed-out readers, or specific groups, and hide it from groups with excludes. See Visibility.

Regional language variants: navigation.languages accepts regional codes such as en-GB, es-MX, and es-419, and the language switcher shows the region. Language routing sends visitors to the variant that matches their browser. See Regional variants.

hreflang tags: Sites with multiple languages link each page to its translations with hreflang tags, so search engines can show readers the right language. See Alternate language links.

TypeDoc categories: SDK reference navigation follows the @category and @group tags in your TypeDoc artifact. See Generated pages.

Preview deployments: The robots.txt file on preview deployments disallows crawling.

Navigation on authenticated sites: Signed-out visitors on sites with authentication see the public navigation on first load, without layout shifts.

Server-rendered custom components: Custom components that you define with export and that only place their props into HTML render on the server, so they no longer pop in after the page loads. See React components.

AI and MCP

Admin MCP comment tools: The admin MCP can read comment threads, start a comment, suggest a tracked change, reply, and resolve threads. See Comments.

Merge from the admin MCP: Pass merge: true to publish to merge the branch's pull request when your project allows edits to the deploy branch. See Branches and publishing.

User ID on MCP events: Search tool calls through an authenticated MCP server record the signed-in user's sub claim as user_id in analytics streaming. Available on Enterprise plans.

Redacted assistant conversations: Email addresses and phone numbers in assistant conversations appear redacted in the dashboard, CSV exports, and the analytics API. Available on Pro and Enterprise plans.

Bug fixes

Editor: Footnotes render instead of showing a warning. Keyboard text selection works across tables. Comment cards stay anchored when you switch tabs, and block menu actions follow their block when content shifts. Autolinked URLs include their paths, queries, and sections and leave out trailing punctuation. Bare domains link to https://. The docs.json tab is titled Site settings.

Comments: The comment popover hides reply and actions when you can't comment. If your organization uses roles, admins can delete any comment or thread.

Published sites: Tabs no longer clip ordered list numbers from 10 up. Related pages pick the right language for index pages.

CLI: mint a11y checks files that use custom heading IDs. mint broken-links reports every page it can't parse instead of stopping at the first, no longer flags valid code inside <MDX> fragments, and resolves relative links in snippets.

Desktop app: Switching organizations no longer switches you back to the previous organization.

Multi-repo: Each GitHub source fetches content through its own installation.

Analytics API: Export date parameters accept ISO 8601 time zone offsets and fractional seconds.

Twenty-three community pull requests: call-resolution and id-collision fixes across JS/TS, Python, Go, Rust and Solidity; graph round-trip, dedup and confidence-folding fixes; skill code-only-update and dispatch fixes; and LLM/Ollama and detection fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: JS/TS class members differing only by _, $ or # are kept as separate nodes (#4475, #4479, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: TypeScript this.field is typed from an assignment in any method, including static and accessors (#4473, #4482, thanks @FolatheDuckofDuckingburg).

Fix: JS a workspace package whose exports points only into dist/ falls back to src/ (#4485, #4489, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: JS a dangling barrel-named import edge is dropped once the import resolves through the barrel (#4486, #4488, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: Python module-level class ids colliding with a function or class are salted apart (#2810, #4467, thanks @hementhu).

Feature: Python a member call on a pytest fixture parameter is typed from the fixture's returned class (#4332, #4333, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: Go / Rust same-file declarations differing only by case are kept as separate nodes (#4468, thanks @abdulsamie10).

Feature: Solidity inherited calls, super calls and modifiers resolve through C3 linearization (#4379, #4384, thanks @rohit-jsfreaky).

Fix: MCP parallel edges are preserved through the graph.json round-trip and query output (#4500, #4503, thanks @rtmalikian).

Fix: dedup a node with a source_file beats a sourceless namesake in collision rank (#4492, #4496, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: build model-drifted string confidences fold to a valid value before validation and dedup (#4495, #4501, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Fix: extractors the in-flight scan root is shared via the extractors base module, restoring the one-way import direction (#3666, #3758, thanks @abhay-codes07).

Fix: detect only a valid .git is treated as a VCS root, so a stray home-dir .git no longer leaks its .gitignore (#4444, #4464, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: hooks post-merge rebuilds on real merges, and a new post-rewrite hook rebuilds after cherry-pick/rebase/pull --rebase (#4463, #4476; #4490, #4491, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill the code-only --update path materializes the extraction before the merge across all hosts (#4447, #4313, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra; aider/devin #4456, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill stray backticks inside a double-quoted -c block no longer run a command mid-step (#4461, #4462, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: skill Pi dispatches semantic subagents to the native delegate agent (#4494, #4502, thanks @bercedev).

Fix: skill the agent pushes to the exact Neo4j/FalkorDB URI supplied, not a localhost example (#4349, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra).

Fix: llm the extraction prompt pins source_file to the dispatched file (#3377, #2270, #4487, thanks @cornwe19).

Feature: llm opt-in backend selection via GRAPHIFY_BACKEND, a disable switch, and an honest auto-detect (#4361, #4376, thanks @nothariharan).

Fix: deps cap tree-sitter-dm <0.26 so a fresh install cannot pull the ABI-incompatible 0.26 grammar (#4044, thanks @safishamsi).

items.text:
0.9.90 (2026-10-13)

Fourteen community pull requests: C# call-resolution and id-collision fixes, Python/Go/dedup correctness, a hub-label sidecar, a post-merge heal hook, and query/build fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Fix: C# a nameless member-call receiver (run.Sequence.Apply(), Make().Apply()) no longer mis-binds to the caller's own same-named method; every C# member call defers and resolves only through a typed receiver (#4422, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Fix: C# new X() no longer binds to a method that shares the type's name, same-file or cross-file; a real same-named type still wins (#4428, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Feature: C# foreach loop variables are now typed from the collection's element type (arrays, known sequences, dictionary .Keys/.Values), so calls on the loop variable resolve; untypable iterables stay unresolved (#4423, thanks @nixvideojuego-ui).

Fix: C# node ids now keep names that differ only by a leading/trailing _ or by case apart (Action/_Action, Load/load, Token/TOKEN), in both ids and member-call resolution keys, instead of collapsing one onto the other (#4415, #4416, thanks @JensD-git).

Fix: C# colliding ids are salted before the partial-class merge, so a partial half keeps its members and an unrelated node sharing a half's id is no longer deleted (#4411, #4412, thanks @JensD-git).

Fix: Go a generic receiver type (func (b *Box[T]) ...) is normalized before building its id, so a generic type's methods attach to the type node instead of a separate Box[T] node (#4438, thanks @Goodkamalpandey).

Fix: Python a module member call (mod.func()) now resolves when the caller is a method or nested function, by walking the enclosing scopes to the file node instead of reading only the immediate parent (#2447, #4437, thanks @SrijanSriv).

Fix: an edge between two surviving nodes is no longer dropped just because its own source_file was not dispatched this run; it is kept as long as both endpoints are kept nodes (#2276, #4436, thanks @SrijanSriv).

Fix: dedup keeps a dropped-folder document next to a top-level file that mints the same id (protocol.md beside docs/protocol.md and docs/firmware/protocol.md), path-qualifying the siblings instead of collapsing and losing one; a genuine reference still collapses onto the named file (#4281, #4410, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah).

Fix: Jinja templates (.j2, .jinja, .jinja2) are now classified as documents instead of being dropped from the graph (#3427, #3455, thanks @nikhilsaxena04).

Fix: build source-less placeholder nodes orphaned by a re-extraction that drops their edges are now swept on a normal (non-prune) incremental build, not just under prune; the sweep removes only code placeholders and external stubs and spares disk-isolated, fresh-isolated, and hyperedge-member nodes (#4399, thanks @Mpasha17).

Fix: query the fallback traversal now retains relationships among the visited nodes (seed-to-seed edges, cycles, cross-links, and parallel relations), via the induced subgraph, instead of printing only tree edges (#4314, #4315, thanks @vibhanshu-mishra).

Feature: watch hub-fallback community labels now go to a .graphify_labels.pending.json sidecar, so the tracked .graphify_labels.json holds only curated (manual/LLM) names; a promoted name drops from the sidecar and an emptied sidecar is removed (#3334, #3551, thanks @ayushcodes10).

Feature: hooks graphify hook install now also installs a post-merge hook that runs an unscoped background rebuild after a merge, healing a symbol the graph.json union merge driver resurrected on one side (which nothing else would re-extract), so the phantom node no longer persists (#2418, #3556, thanks @ayushcodes10).

0.9.89 (2026-10-13)

Sixteen community pull requests: cross-repo member-call resolution (Go, PHP, TypeScript, Kotlin, Objective-C), generic/template type-parameter cleanup (Kotlin, Scala, C++, Swift), an Objective-C enum extractor, interface-dispatch fan-out, a native Pi guard extension, and several resolution/ingest fixes. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

Feature: cross-repo member calls now finish across a repository boundary for Go, PHP, TypeScript/JS, Kotlin and Objective-C: a call whose receiver type is declared in another repo is parked by name during the single-repo build and bound on merge-graphs/global add against a unique same-named exported type, fail-closed on ambiguity (#3152, #3388, #3393, #3385, #3387, #3389, #3391, #3395, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: Go a package's type whose methods span several files now folds into one node instead of fragmenting under _disambiguate_colliding_node_ids, so single-definition guards and receiver typing work (#3399, #3400, thanks @xiongjianxu).

Fix: Kotlin / Scala / C++ / Swift generic and template type parameters (class Box<T>, [T], template<typename T>, struct Stack<Element>) no longer mint sourceless stub god-nodes; a real same-named type is still referenced (#4406, #4407, #4408, #4409, thanks @rajatnagda45).

Feature: Objective-C NS_ENUM and NS_OPTIONS declarations are now extracted as an enum type plus its members, with the macro forms validated and malformed macros rejected fail-closed (#4400, #4401, thanks @oleksii-tumanov).

Feature: dispatch an interface member now links to every implementer, not just one, so a DI chain through a multi-implementer interface resolves; the fan-out is gated to genuine implementers with a correct method match (#3800, #4396, thanks @Goodkamalpandey).

Feature: Pi a native Pi guard extension now runs graphify hook-guard before Pi's tool calls and also loads under Oh My Pi, so the hook-guard policy reaches Pi; install/uninstall delegates to pi install/pi remove and the guard fails open (#4378, thanks @andrebrait).

v4.1.0: Fourth and One

FastMCP 4.1.0 is a maintenance release at heart: a broad sweep of fixes across OpenAPI, proxies, auth, tasks, and the CLI, plus full Python 3.15 support. It doesn't change how most servers behave. A few security fixes do tighten inputs that FastMCP previously accepted, though, and our versioning policy keeps breaking changes out of patch releases, so this ships as a point-one release.

Check these before upgrading:

MultiAuth now qualifies client IDs by source, so existing MultiAuth sessions and tasks start new ownership scopes. Finish pending tasks before upgrading.

Regex tool search uses Pydantic's regex engine, which doesn't support lookarounds or backreferences.

Skill files must resolve inside their configured directories.

OpenAPI path parameters reject . and .. segments.

HTTP sessions now expire after the MCP SDK's 30-minute idle default instead of never.

CodeMode requires Monty 1.1, which renames max_duration_secs to max_feed_duration_secs.

Desktop app

Deep links: mintlify:// links open in the desktop app as a new tab.

Zoom and new tabs: Zoom in, zoom out, or reset the zoom from the View menu. Cmd + N opens a new tab with a blank page.

Offline screen: Navigation changes you made while offline save when your connection returns. The app shows an offline screen if you lose your connection.

Find in page: Press Cmd + F to search the current page. See Keyboard shortcuts for more information.

Check for updates: Check for a new version from the app menu or settings. See Updates for more information.

Browser sign-in: Sign in to the desktop app through your default browser. If browser sign-in isn't available for your organization, sign in inside the app. See Sign in for more information.

Agent and AI

Agent replies to comments: The agent can read open comments and suggestions on a page, reply to threads, and resolve comment threads.

Google Docs integration: Connect Google Docs as a read-only personal integration so the agent can search and read your documents. Available on Enterprise plans.

Admin MCP: The admin MCP can edit your deploy branch directly when the branch doesn't require pull requests. It can also upload images and returns links to private pages. The diff shows who made each pending change.

items.title: Agent Frameworks Compared: Tool-Calling Schema Handling
items.text: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google each use a different request and response shape for the same tool. Agent frameworks handle that difference in different places. Some translate one definition into each provider's format, some are native to a single provider, and some hand the question to a connector underneath. This article compares six frameworks on schema definition, translation, and MCP support, then shows how OpenRouter normalizes tool calling at the API layer so a model swap is a change to one string.

items.title: LangChain vs CrewAI: Orchestration Compared to OpenRouter-Native Routing
items.text: Multi-model orchestration is three layers. Workflow orchestration is planning, state, memory, and delegation, and LangGraph and CrewAI are built for it. This article separates the layers, shows the same two-step pipeline in direct OpenRouter calls and in LangChain, and describes when to add a framework, when to use our Agent SDK, and how to put OpenRouter underneath LangGraph or CrewAI.

AI credit pricing updates

Fixed credits for assistant answers: Each assistant answer uses 25 credits.

Fixed automation pricing: All automations use 250 credits per successful run. If an automation fails or finds nothing to update, it uses zero credits.

Free editor and Slack agent: Using the agent in the editor or Slack does not use credits for Pro and Enterprise plans.

OpenAPI Overlays

Transform a spec: Use OpenAPI Overlays to rename paths, replace server URLs, or remove internal endpoints without editing the specification file. Overlays apply after a specification is parsed and before it is validated, so generated endpoint pages, navigation, openapi frontmatter, and mint validate all use the transformed document. See Transform your spec with overlays.

Overlay Specification 1.0 and 1.1: Write update, remove, and copy actions that select nodes with RFC 9535 JSONPath expressions. See Create an overlay document.

Reference or auto-discover overlays: Add an overlays property anywhere your docs.json accepts openapi, using a relative path or a URL. Or skip the configuration: an overlay with an extends field pointing at your specification is discovered automatically. See Auto-discover overlays.

Editor and collaboration

Recent and starred private pages: The Workspace tab of the editor now lists the private pages you opened most recently and the ones you star from a page's menu. Both lists sync across your devices and stay the same on every branch. Each section stays hidden until it has something in it. You can reorder these sidebar groups by dragging them to create your preferred workspace layout.

Move and duplicate private pages: Move a private page into a workspace folder from its document or sidebar menu, duplicate a private page from the same menu, or leave a private page you were invited to. When you promote a private page, its images and videos move with it and inline references are rewritten. See Private pages.

Comments panel: Open a document-wide comments panel to review open and resolved threads for the current page. Source mode now supports comments the same as visual mode. See Comments.

Resize table columns: In visual mode, drag a column border to resize it. The editor converts the table to HTML and writes the <colgroup> widths for you. See Tables.

Site settings in the sidebar: Site configuration pages open directly from the editor sidebar instead of a modal, and workspace settings navigation has been reorganized to match.

Page icons as tab favicons: The editor tab favicon now uses the page's icon. Page and navigation icon frontmatter accept emoji values.

Automations

Automatic merge conflict resolution: When an automation's pull request has merge conflicts, the agent can resolve them for you, either automatically or when you click Accept on the pull request. See Resolve merge conflicts.

Manual pull request runs: Manually triggered runs against a specific pull request are now labeled as such in the runs feed, and the runs page shows run count badges, unified result cards, and a simpler summary. See Manage automations.

Published sites

Image viewer: Clicking an image opens a rebuilt full-size viewer with smoother animation and labeled controls for screen readers.

Search ranking: Search ranks page-title matches higher, so exact-title lookups surface first.

Dashboard

Workspace and organization icons: Upload a workspace icon from your general settings and an organization icon from your organization settings. See Change your workspace icon.

IP-blocked error page: Requests blocked by an IP allowlist now land on a dedicated error page that explains what happened.

Git and integrations

Non-Markdown files sync in the editor: Editor branches now sync non-MDX text files, so changes to config files and other plain-text assets round-trip through the editor.

GitLab editor branches: GitLab pushes sync into editor branches in real time, contributors show on the branch dropdown, and force pushes are detected. Git-only branches now appear in the editor branch dropdown so you can switch to a branch that was created outside the editor.

Default ignored patterns: .vscode and .cursor are ignored by default, and mint dev skips ignored directories when it crawls your project. See Default ignored patterns.

API playground

Playground labels: The oneOf variant dropdown uses title-aware labels so each option is easier to identify.

Bug fixes

Preview deployments: GitHub preview deployments are pinned to the triggering commit, preview URLs stay stable across rebuilds, and preview comments refresh after each rebuild.

Custom domains and 404s: Custom hostnames Cloudflare no longer serves return not_found, MCP analytics resolve custom domains to their canonical subdomain, and Markdown 404s include recovery guidance and discovery headers.

Components: RequestExample and ResponseExample code blocks no longer disappear on small screens.

Editor fixes: Creating a branch no longer leaves a stuck skeleton, pull-request link redirects no longer double-encode branch names, saving rows match the server, resizing no longer loops, and frontmatter loads only after the document connects.

Publishing: Content-less create actions retire after publish so they cannot block later publishes, publish retries when the branch lock is held instead of erroring immediately, and GitHub commit failures report clearer messages.

items.title: Notification preferences, collaborative source mode, and more
items.text:
Notification preferences

Notification preferences: Choose which emails you receive for each event, including comment replies and mentions, thread resolutions, suggestions submitted, accepted, or rejected, automation runs, and product feedback. Configure preferences on the Notifications page of your dashboard.

Automation failure emails: Turn on automation run notifications to get an email when a run fails. Mintlify then holds further failure emails until a run succeeds again.

Share notifications: Mintlify notifies you when someone shares a page with you.

Editor and collaboration

Collaborative source mode: Source mode now supports real-time collaboration. See your teammates' cursors as they work on the same branch as you. Frontmatter edits sync live across visual and source mode. See Real-time editing.

Comment reactions: React to a comment with an emoji to acknowledge it without replying. Hover over a reaction to see who reacted, and reacting to someone else's comment notifies its author. See Comments.

Selective publish: Select individual changes in the publish menu to publish part of your pending work instead of everything at once.

Media on private pages: Upload images and videos to private pages. Private media is served only to people who can open the page, and it is removed when the page is deleted.

Editor polish: Search results show page titles and reveal the file in the sidebar, the sidebar lists only Markdown pages by default, the share dialog searches recipients by email address, the emoji suggestion menu has better search relevance, and the agent panel stays available in site settings.

Automations

Run scope for manual runs: When you trigger an automation manually, choose whether it reviews changes since a date, the entire site, or a specific pull request. See Run an automation manually.

Analytics

Page filter: Filter your analytics to a specific page with the new page dropdown in the dashboard.

API playground

Optional field toggles: In the playground modal, required fields sort first and optional fields collapse behind an Expand N optional fields control, with a global toggle in the header. Collapsed fields stay findable. Searching the page for a hidden field name expands the section that contains it, and values you entered persist across collapse and expand.

Collapse fields by default: Set expand: false under x-mint: playground on an operation to collapse nested object fields by default. See Collapse playground fields.

Authoring

mint test: Generate tests for the code blocks in your docs from the CLI. Runs are saved so you can revisit past reports. See mint test.

<MDX> improvements: Headings inside <MDX> blocks merge into the page's table of contents, ## Title {#id} anchors work at any indent, and code blocks inside <MDX> behave like code blocks at the page root. See MDX.

Markdown in component titles: Component titles, such as accordion titles, support inline Markdown formatting like code and bold.

Table column widths: HTML tables honor the <colgroup> widths you author.

Referrals

Enterprise referrals: Enterprise organizations can now participate in the referral program.

Bug fixes

Static exports: Static builds bundle your logo files so exported sites no longer reference missing assets.

GitLab subgroups: Repositories in nested GitLab subgroups sync correctly.

Large repositories: Repositories large enough that GitHub truncates their file listing now sync all files.

Assistant citations: Citations that dropped a leading path segment now open the correct page.

Authenticated previews: Preview deployments for docs behind authentication serve your changed files.

Translations: The translation automation writes locale-prefixed internal links, so newly translated pages link within their own language.

OpenAPI cleanup: Deleting an OpenAPI spec removes its generated assets from your site.

Custom fonts: Bold text stays bold when you set a custom body font weight.

Code feedback: The code snippet feedback popover displays above the table of contents panel.

Dismissed banners: Dismissed banners no longer flash on page load.

Editor fixes: Reference-style links and Link components render correctly, HTML tables with colspan or classes round-trip without changes, editing a page no longer reformats untouched content, and branch switching no longer causes redirect loops.

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.23 — Reasoning content and tool‑calling reliability
items.text: For gpt‑oss on POST /v1/chat/completions , reasoning content moves out of message.content and into choices.message.reasoning (non‑streaming) and choices.delta.reasoning (streaming), aligning with o3‑mini ‡ . Tool names are normalized (e.g., snake_case) before being provided to the model to improve tool‑calling reliability ‡ . Fixed errors for certain tools‑containing requests to POST /v1/chat/completions (e.g., "reading 'properties'") and non‑streaming tool‑call failures ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.19 — Bug fixes for streaming and tool calls
items.text: Corrected usage statistics returned by OpenAI‑compatible streaming responses ‡ . Improved handling of parallel tool calls via the streaming API ‡ . Fixed parsing of correct tool calls for certain Mistral models ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.18 — Streaming options and tool‑calling improvements
items.text: Added support for the stream_options object on OpenAI‑compatible endpoints. Setting stream_options.include_usage to true returns prompt and completion token usage during streaming ‡ . Errors returned from streaming endpoints now follow the correct format expected by OpenAI clients ‡ . Tool‑calling support added for Mistral v13 tokenizer models, using proper chat templates ‡ . The response_format.type field now accepts "text" in chat‑completion requests ‡ . Fixed bugs where parallel tool calls split across multiple chunks were dropped and where root‑level $defs in tool definitions were stripped ‡ .

items.title: LM Studio 0.3.17 — Tool‑calling reliability and token‑count updates
items.text: Token counts now include the system prompt and tool definitions ‡ . This makes usage reporting more accurate for both the UI and the API. Tool‑call argument tokens are streamed as they are generated ‡ , improving responsiveness when using streamed function calls. Various fixes improve MCP and tool‑calling reliability, including correct handling of tools that omit a parameters object and preventing hangs when an MCP server reloads ‡ .
